item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after board reversal
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer, reversing its earlier position on his departure. The company's board of directors voted unanimously to restore Huang to the positions, effective immediately, and reinstate him as a board member, the company announced on November 23.
The decision followed a series of discussions between Huang and the board, which said it was satisfied with his candor and leadership capabilities. The board also consulted senior US government officials and concluded that Huang's return would pose no national security risk.
Jensen Huang gives a keynote address at the Nvidia Berlin GPU Technology Conference in Berlin, Germany, October 21, 2026. /VCG
Board Chair Harvey C. Jones said Huang was the right person to lead Nvidia and that his reinstatement was in the best interests of the company's shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Jones will remain board chair. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's absence, will continue in her role as chief financial officer.
Huang voluntarily resigned on November 12 after the board raised concerns about his personal conduct, which it said was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and corporate culture. At Nvidia's quarterly earnings call on November 17, Jones said the board had unanimously accepted the resignation and did not intend to reinstate Huang. Kress was appointed interim CEO, and the company began searching for a permanent successor.
The board's latest decision came after a wave of public support for Huang's return. Reuters reported that a petition calling for his reinstatement had attracted more than 180,000 signatures, including one from Tesla CEO Elon Musk. US President Donald Trump, who had urged Nvidia to bring Huang back the previous week, welcomed the board's decision on Monday, calling it the "correct and proper decision" in a post on Truth Social. Trump also said the US government had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk and urged Nvidia to continue ensuring compliance with US export controls.
Despite Huang's return, an independent investigation launched by the board will continue. Nvidia said the committee overseeing the inquiry, composed entirely of independent directors and supported by outside legal counsel, would carry its investigation through to completion. Huang has pledged full cooperation.
The company has also established a separate National Security and Export Control Committee, made up exclusively of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging legal counsel with relevant expertise, while Nvidia is seeking to appoint a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance across the company and report to the board's Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.
Nvidia said it would continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

item.title: China to launch Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Nov. 25
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday.
A Long March-2F carrier rocket, which will be used for the launch, will soon be filled with propellant, said Zhang Jingbo, the CMSA spokesperson, at a press conference.
Shenzhou-24 is the eighth crewed mission during the application and development stage of China's space station, and the 41st flight mission of China's manned space program.

item.title: Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping extended congratulations to a UN meeting held on Monday to commemorate the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People.
In his message, Xi said that the Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, adding that the current tensions in the Middle East should not divert the international community's attention from the Palestinian issue. The key to resolving the Palestinian question is to stay on course toward the two-state solution and promote the resumption of peace talks between Palestine and Israel, Xi said.
He stressed that the governance of the West Bank and post-war reconstruction in Gaza should be advanced in accordance with the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine," and opposed any land-grabbing or rights-infringing actions targeting the Palestinian people.
The international community should translate its consensus and commitments in support of Palestine into concrete actions, promote a lasting ceasefire in Gaza and protect the safety of civilians, Xi said.
Xi said that justice will prevail and must not be absent. China has always firmly supported the just cause of the Palestinian people to restore their legitimate national rights, he said.
China will continue to work with all countries that cherish peace and uphold justice to promote the early realization of a comprehensive, just and lasting solution of the Palestinian question, based on the rule of international law and with a view to addressing both its symptoms and root causes, Xi said.
Such efforts will contribute to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and make positive contributions to world peace, stability, development and prosperity, Xi added.

item.title: U.S. stocks surge as Nvidia's Huang reinstatement reignites AI trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
This undated file photo shows an exterior view of the NVIDIA headquarters in Santa Clara, California, the United States. (Xinhua)
NEW YORK, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- U.S. stocks surged on Monday as Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and CEO reignited the AI trade, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite posting their biggest single-day gains since April 9, 2025.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,447.98 points, or 3.01 percent, to 49,595.31. The S&P 500 added 326.78 points, or 4.73 percent, to 7,237.17. The Nasdaq Composite Index increased by 1,471.83 points, or 6.51 percent, to 24,089.56.
Nine of the 11 primary S&P 500 sectors ended higher, with technology leading the gainers by adding 9.03 percent, while energy led the laggards by falling 1.32 percent.
Oil prices fell sharply as concerns over a global supply glut outweighed risks to supplies from the Middle East. West Texas Intermediate crude for January delivery dropped 3.88 percent to settle at 80.17 U.S. dollars a barrel, its lowest level since August, while Brent crude fell 3.46 percent to 89.37 dollars a barrel.
On the corporate front, Nvidia surged 31.48 percent after its board unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately. The chipmaker recorded the largest single-day increase in market capitalization on record, adding nearly 1 trillion dollars and bringing its valuation back close to 4 trillion dollars.
Chip stocks rallied across the board, with Micron Technology jumping around 19 percent, Marvell Technology up 18.37 percent, and Intel climbing 16.34 percent. Advanced Micro Devices gained 6.85 percent, while Dell Technologies rocketed over 20 percent. CoreWeave popped 22.32 percent and Oracle jumped 12.34 percent.
"The shocking decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO helps to remove a key level of uncertainty from the AI trade, which has been suffering in recent weeks," said Glen Smith, chief investment officer at GDS Wealth Management. The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street's fear gauge, fell nearly 26 percent to 26.62.
The rally in chip stocks also lifted other technology shares. Tesla surged 11.46 percent, while Alphabet and Meta Platforms each jumped over 6 percent.
On the economic front, S&P Global's flash Purchasing Managers' Index showed U.S. business activity growth easing to a four-month low in November. The composite index fell to 54.6 from 55.9 in October, while the services index slipped to 54.7 and the manufacturing index fell to 54.5.
Investors also continued to weigh the prospect of a quarter-point interest rate hike at the Fed's December meeting, with the October personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, due for release on Wednesday.

item.title: China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. (Xinhua)
JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday.
The three astronauts are a spacecraft pilot, a flight engineer and a payload specialist, respectively. Tang has participated in the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 crewed flight missions and is about to become the first astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station three times. Wu comes from the country's third batch of astronauts and will embark on his first spaceflight mission. Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong.
China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson of the agency, said at a press conference.

item.title: Hong Kong announces results of 2026 Election Committee subsector elections
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
HONG KONG, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- Results of the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) were announced on Sunday evening, with all 723 Election Committee seats across 31 subsectors filled after being contested by 856 candidates.
Under the electoral arrangements, 341 individuals were confirmed as validly registered as ex-officio members of the Election Committee, while 156 were confirmed as validly nominated members. In addition, 259 candidates were returned uncontested, while 856 candidates contested 723 seats on Sunday.
Following the announcement of the election results, John Lee, chief executive of the HKSAR, said in a statement on Sunday evening that the elections fully demonstrated a healthy competition among patriots who are committed, competent and constructive, highlighting the positivity of democratic development under the principle of "patriots administering Hong Kong."
Lee expected that in accordance with the principle, all Election Committee members will fulfil their duties diligently and responsibly, and contribute to the steady and sustained implementation of the "one country, two systems" principle.
The Election Committee is an important part of the HKSAR's electoral system. According to Annexes I and II to the HKSAR Basic Law, the Election Committee, composed of 1,500 members, shall be responsible for electing the Chief Executive-designate and some members of the HKSAR's Legislative Council (LegCo). The Election Committee shall also be responsible for nominating candidates for the posts of Chief Executive and LegCo members.
The new Election Committee will serve a five-year term from Feb. 1, 2027, to Jan. 31, 2032.

item.title: China's tech innovation engine powers a connected Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
An APEC-themed installation is seen on Xiangmihu road in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)
* China's push to unleash the potential of innovation and share technological dividends through open regional integration has resonated widely -- translating its innovation capacity into broader market opportunities and lending fresh momentum to economic growth and the building of an Asia-Pacific community.
* Across the Asia-Pacific, China's technological innovations are finding applications in a growing range of industries and aspects of everyday life.
* The release of the Shenzhen Initiative marked a milestone in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit. It was a historic moment in Shenzhen, a city that has stood at the forefront of China's opening-up and has grown into a global innovation hub.
BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- As host of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China has placed openness, innovation and cooperation at the heart of its agenda as the three priority areas. Throughout this week's sessions, participants explored how the Asia-Pacific can navigate structural shifts and cultivate new engines of economic growth.
INNOVATION THAT BENEFITS ALL
At an experimental durian orchard at Chiang Mai University in Thailand, agricultural lecturer Supakorn Wongsuk prepares a drone for takeoff. Having studied in China, he now applies the technology to explore more efficient methods of cultivating tropical fruits.
Lifting smoothly into the air, the drone glides above rows of durian trees, releasing a fine mist of pesticide across their leaves and branches.
"Using drones to spray pesticides can improve operational efficiency, reduce farmers' direct exposure to chemicals, and protect their health and safety," said Supakorn.
He sees the Chinese innovations as offering benefits that extend well beyond farming efficiency. "For young people, drone operations can also create new job opportunities."
The role of innovation also drew sharp focus at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen.
"Innovation is very important, and innovation cannot be done overnight. It requires strong education support and accumulated experience. This is where we think China can play a role," said Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Anindya N. Bakrie.
"China has an important role to play," said Julien Leclair-Dionne, associate director at the University of Ottawa's Professional Development Institute. "Particularly given its technological capabilities, innovation ecosystem and experience in scaling emerging technologies."
An AI trainer operates a robot to collect data at a humanoid robot innovation center in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Nov. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Zhizun)
"Ultimately, what matters most is not simply how advanced the technologies become, but how effectively the innovations are translated into opportunities for people, organizations and communities across the region," he said.
OPENNESS CREATES OPPORTUNITIES
Released on Wednesday, the Shenzhen Initiative of the APEC CEO Summit 2026 highlighted the transformative potential of frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence, while recognizing the accompanying risks and regulatory challenges that require coordinated regional oversight.
At the heart of the document lies a clear, unified conviction among business leaders: no single economy can capture the promise of breakthrough technology -- or tame its disruptions -- alone; only deep regional cooperation can turn innovation into shared prosperity.
Auckland Business Chamber CEO Simon Bridges emphasized the need for cooperation amid global uncertainty. "I think cooperation is probably the byword of APEC. And we know in the world right now, it's more important than ever," he said.
China's approach to AI development provides "a very good example" that allows others to learn from its technological advances, he added.
The appeal of Chinese AI models has become increasingly evident across the region. In South Korea, nearly half of the AI models released by local developers on Hugging Face, a globally popular open-source platform, between January and August this year were based on Chinese foundation models.
"China has adopted AI with more open-weight, open-source, low-cost models that are going to be used by businesses around the world," said Jacob Cooke, CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies, a leading e-commerce and technology consultancy.
"These Chinese companies have done their best to get this technology out to help people," Cooke said at the summit.
The opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 is held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
For Lee Ju-kwan, director of the National Center for APEC Studies at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy of South Korea, Shenzhen's relentless innovation engine came vividly into focus during a visit to electric vehicle giant BYD's headquarters, offering a firsthand look at the homegrown tech muscle powering the city.
"I was deeply impressed by what I saw, particularly robots performing tasks that would traditionally be carried out by human workers on the production line," Lee said.
"This year, by hosting APEC, China has taken the opportunity to put forward and renew initiatives aimed at promoting openness and cooperation. I believe these efforts deserve attention and support," Lee said.
GREEN INNOVATION
"It's the most fantastic ride," said Jeffrey Sachs, a professor at Columbia University, looking back on an epic 15,000-km summer odyssey from Rome to China's Hong Kong, retracing Marco Polo's historic path behind the wheel of a BYD electric vehicle.
This photo taken on Sept. 9, 2026 shows an assembly line at the BYD Fuzhou base in Fuzhou, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang)
Sachs said the journey showed how far green technology had advanced. "The technology is already here. Most of it is in its most advanced stage in China," Sachs said during a high-level panel at the APEC CEO Summit 2026.
He also noted that China had significantly reduced the cost of green technologies, making the transition more affordable. "To go green is not to make an extra burden for the sake of the planet. It's just to have a low-cost, resilient, state-of-the-art energy system," he said.
The benefits of China's green innovation are also being felt by residents of Goulburn in New South Wales, Australia. With an integrated solar-and-storage solution supplied by a Chinese company, the local community has brought its own solar farm into operation.
The facility began supplying electricity to the grid in March, with part of its annual profits to be channeled into a community fund to help residents facing energy poverty.
"For a long time, it has been talk around the kitchen table. Suddenly here we are in amongst the panels, watching the sun send electrons to the people and my kids all own little parts of this with the community," said Goulburn resident Dave Suttle.
"Without China's involvement, we definitely wouldn't have solar cells as cheap as now," Martin Green, Scientia Professor of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering at the University of New South Wales, told Xinhua.
Having worked with China's photovoltaic industry for more than four decades, Green is now collaborating with Chinese partners on the next generation of solar technology.
"Working with China, we feel we're in a position to improve the solar performance more quickly," he said.

item.title: Why Global Visitors Are Flocking to Chinese EVs in Shenzhen?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
From automated parking and tank turns to ultra-fast charging in extreme cold, each technological breakthrough is redefining what's possible in the automotive industry. But beyond the technology itself lies something even more significant: China's innovation speed, R&D capabilities, and industrial strength.
From leading global EV sales to attracting attention from international industry players, China's new energy vehicle sector is making a major leap—from exporting products to expanding its technological influence worldwide.
One car reflects the rise of an entire industry. And what's driving onto the global stage is the strength of Chinese manufacturing and innovation.
